utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will the Registrar call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-03-69-PT, the Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. For the Prosecution, Dermot Groome, accompanied by David Re, Melissa Pack, Skye Winner and Rachel Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the Defence, Mr. Knoops, lead counsel; Mr. Jordash, co-counsel; Stephan Karganovic, the case manager; and in our midst is also Dr. Tarabar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the witness comes in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was saying that before the witness comes in, I will give some rulings on applications that have been made. I have to say that I detect an element of opportunism in the filings of these very late applications for evidence in this case, which has been around for some time. The Prosecutor has filed an application to admit the Prosecutor's report in relation to the letter filed by the President to the Security Council. As the Simatovic case has already closed, it would not be right to admit this, this report. And the Kostunica interview, for the same reason, it would not be proper to admit this since the Simatovic case has already closed. In relation to the filings by the Defence, the Chamber will, as is its practice, deal with these filings and the admission of particular statements at the end of the case and will do so after hearing from the Prosecutor on the various statements. However, in relation to the application for the admission of a statement by the accused, that is rejected. It is, of course, open to the accused to give evidence if he wishes to do so, and in any event, counsel can address us on this matter in his closing address. We have set out the schedule for the hearing of these witnesses. And it's half an hour for each witness, half an hour for examination-in-chief, half an hour for cross-examination, and if we are to get through them, we have to follow this. We have to inject some rigour into it, and Mr. Knoops, I want you to bear this in mind. We have to proceed judiciously, but as quickly as possible. And your witness is Dr. Offermans, the first witness. Mr. Knoops.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Defence wants to hear Dr. Offermans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KNOOPS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence request to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
